messages:
cj: Heads up — experimenting with a 'bundled' exporter mode in our SDKs for inference services. Goals: reduce TCP churn to collectors, enforce per-tenant retention hints, and make backpressure deterministic. Thoughts on queueing policy across Python/Go/Rust?

maya: Love the idea. Main ops concerns: worker process shutdown (gunicorn/uvicorn), memory drift in long-lived handlers, and ensuring per-tenant headers don't leak.

alex: For Go we've used a bounded async queue with drop-oldest + a counter for drops. Pretty simple:
```go
queue := make(chan *export.Span, 1000)
go func() {
  for s := range queue { exporter.Export(s) }
}()
```
We expose REDWOOD_OTEL_QUEUE_SIZE and a high/low watermark.

sam: Python is trickier with the GIL. Our current pattern is a local unix-socket daemon exporter to avoid blocking workers — workers push spans to socket, daemon batches and talks to OTLP. Also need SIGHUP/SIGTERM drain and post-fork handling.

lina: Rust approach: tokio mpsc bounded channel + a BufferPool. We apply exponential backoff on exporter errors and flip to a sample-only mode when queue exceeds high watermark. Also we avoid copying huge attribute maps by using Arc refs.

cj: How should retention_hint / per-tenant retention be expressed? OTLP attributes on every span will bloat. Maybe send tenant retention as a resource attribute during connection bootstrap or attach to batch-level metadata.

maya: @alex we also need per-tenant auth headers for collector — can the bundler attach headers per-batch? Otherwise multi-tenant sidecars need to be tenant-aware.

alex: We batch and set headers at batch time in the Go exporter. That requires the exporter/agent to carry tenant context; we surface that via an envelope metadata struct.

sam: Ops-wise I'd prefer a sidecar/agent to consolidate headers & retention rules, but we must keep a direct-export option for Private deployments. Sidecar also helps with credential rotation.

cj: Important: graceful fallback when exporter overloads. Proposal: when queueFull -> switch sampling to low rate, increment metric otel.export.dropped, and emit an alert. Pseudocode:
```py
if queue_full:
  sampler.set_rate(0.1)
  metrics.increment('otel.export.dropped')
```

agent-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployed otel-bundled mode to staging (region-us-east-2) at 03:15 UTC — no ingest regressions in 2h :white_check_mark:

lina: Also document shutdown handshake variance per language. Prefer a non-blocking 'flush with timeout' that returns quickly for main thread but continues background flush. Expose OTEL_EXPORTER_FLUSH_TIMEOUT_MS.

cj: Agreed. Next steps: I'll draft a 1-pager spec and proposed API for 'bundled' mode + example configs for Python/Go/Rust. Will open a PR. Assigning reviewers @maya @alex @lina.

maya: :thumbsup: Can we include a migration path: REDWOOD_OTELOPTION=legacy|bundled and a rollout flag in Console so we can stage per-customer?

alex: SG. I'll add Go SDK tests for header attachment, queue watermarks, and exporter backoff behavior.

sam: I'll prototype the Python unix-socket daemon + benchmark sync vs socket vs bundled and share numbers.

cj: Thanks all. If anyone has concrete failure modes (post-fork leaks, sock permissions, TLS per-tenant), drop them here and I'll fold into the spec.
